name: Can I remain living in the house while my floor plan is being reconfigured?

mainEntity.name: Can I remain living in the house while my floor plan is being reconfigured?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether you can stay in your home depends heavily on the scale of the layout changes and which rooms are affected. If the reconfiguration focuses primarily on a main-floor kitchen, living area, or primary suite, families often remain living on a different floor or in an unaffected basement. However, moving structural walls, cutting into subfloors, and rerouting main electrical panels or whole-home water supplies brings significant noise, dust, and brief utility shutdowns. When a whole-home reconfiguration cuts off functional kitchens and bathrooms simultaneously, temporary off-site accommodation is generally recommended.
acceptedAnswer.description: You can often stay if work is isolated to one area, but extensive reconfigurations affecting main utilities, kitchens, or multiple bathrooms usually favor temporary relocation.
